clues.text: This city sits in northern Iran, between the Caspian Sea coast and the mountains. It is the largest city on that whole coast.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northern Iran and the Caspian coast

source.quote: Rasht is the largest city on Iran's Caspian Sea coast. Due to being between the coast and the mountains, the local environment is rainy with a humid subtropical climate.

clues.text: Rain falls a lot here because the city sits between the sea and the mountains. Just south is a green rain forest, while most of Iran is dry.
clues.narrowing: rules out dry inland Iran and points to the wet coast by the mountains

source.quote: Due to being between the coast and the mountains, the local environment is rainy with a humid subtropical climate. It also has a temperate rainforest to its south, in contrast to the rest of Iran, which is mostly arid.

clues.text: Its past goes back to the 1200s. Much later, in Safavid times, it was a main hub for silk, with many cloth workshops.
clues.narrowing: rules out coast cities that were not old silk trade hubs

source.quote: The city has a history that goes back to the 13th century, but its modern history dates back to the Safavid era during which Rasht was a major center of the silk trade with numerous textile workshops.

clues.text: Traders once called this place the Gate of Europe. Its roads and trade linked Iran with Russia and the rest of Europe.
clues.narrowing: rules out all but the old trade gate linking Iran to Europe

source.quote: Historically, Rasht was a major transport and business center which connected Iran to Russia and the rest of Europe, and because of this it was known as the "Gate of Europe".

clues.text: In 2015 the world named this a top food city. UNESCO put it on its list of creative cities for its cooking.
clues.narrowing: confirms the UNESCO creative food city on that coast

source.quote: In 2015, this city joined the network of creative cities of the world as a creative gastronomy city under the supervision of UNESCO.
